newsitem.title: USA: Dollar recovers ground vs yen, ends higher in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Dollar recovers ground vs yen, ends higher in U.S..

text.p: The dollar ended U.S. trading mostly higher, regaining some of the ground it lost overnight as market players reevaluated a tankan report that initially fueled yen buying, dealers said.

The greenback traded in narrow ranges against most other currencies, but gained on the British pound, with sellers continuing to cite a sterling-bearish report on Tuesday from investment bank Goldman Sachs.
The Bank of Japan's tankan survey showed surging optimism among big Japanese manufacturers, suggesting Japan's huge trade surplus with the United States will continue to grow.

"The tankan was much stronger than anticipated," said John McCarthy, senior vice president at ING Barings. "There's no question we'll see upward pressure on Japanese trade surpluses and slow, but sure upward pressure on the yen."
But after falling more than a yen, the dollar rebounded somewhat as U.S. trading began, with market players focusing on a separate tankan index showing weakness among non-manufacturers.
Underlying Japanese economic weakness might delay any interest rate hikes by the Bank of Japan, which enhances the appeal of more lucrative dollar-linked investments.

"The implication is that the Bank of Japan is on hold, so the downside for the dollar is limited, based on the interest rate differential, which is the main focus of dollar/yen trading," said Mike Malpede, senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group, Ltd.
The dollar closed higher at 113.87/97 yen, up from 113.50/60 at the open, but down from 114.90/95 at Tuesday's close. The greenback ended little changed at 1.7235/45 marks, versus 1.7235/38.

The yen was also aided by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who told a European Union summit in the Hague, Netherlands he hoped Europe's proposed single currency would not reduce international usage of the yen.

A reported 0.6-percent drop in U.S. May durable goods orders contradicted a 4.4-percent gain in May existing home sales, supporting the consensus view that Federal Reserve leaders will hold interest rates steady when they meet next week.
"The U.S. numbers were really offsetting," Malpede said.
The pound fell broadly in Europe amid residual selling after a weekly Goldman Sachs European report called it 15 percent overvalued on Tuesday.
"That put a lot of pressure on sterling, which fell against the dollar and the deutschemark," Malpede added.
In other European trade, the mark fell to its lowest point in five months against the Italian lira.
Widespread rumors that Italian officials would lower interest rates and talk that the lira would be included in the first round of Europe's monetary union boosted the Italian unit, traders said.
"The prospects for Italy to join on the first round are as good as at any time before, so we're seeing continual interest to buy Italian fixed-income instruments," McCarthy said.

In other trade, the dollar fell to 1.4365/75 Swiss francs from 1.4390/00 at the open. The greenback rose to Canadian $1.3935/40 from C$1.3913/18. The Australian dollar fell to $0.7501/06 from $0.7505/10.
